description: Machine-readable data index for aisharedresponsibility.com. All files are static JSON served from /data/. Framework concepts (layers, personas, operating models) are defined in the CoSAI AI Shared Responsibility Framework v1.0.

files.description: The five SRF architecture layers: L1 AI Business & Usage, L2 AI Information, L3 AI Application, L4 AI Platform, L5 AI Model Provider. Each entry includes personas, operating model responsibility assignments, and component descriptions.

The eight SRF personas: AI System Users, AI System Governance, Data Provider, Application Developer, Agentic Platform & Framework Providers, AI Model Serving, AI Platform Provider, Model Provider. Also declares sector_specializations (for example clinical-ai-governance) that specialize a canonical persona; every accountable_persona value in a control file resolves to one of these records.

Responsibility matrix across the four operating models (AI-SaaS, AI-PaaS, Agent-PaaS, IaaS) and five layers. Each cell specifies whether accountability is customer-owned, shared, provider-managed, model-evaluation, or N/A.

Controlled vocabulary for the jurisdiction that issues a regulation or standard. Levels: international (standards bodies), oecd (soft law), supranational (eu), national (us-federal, uk, china, singapore, canada, japan, australia, south-korea, brazil, india), multistate, subnational (us-california, us-colorado, us-new-york). Referenced by the jurisdiction field on each regulations.json item and materialized as srf.jurisdiction.* nodes in the ontology.

AI regulations and standards mapped to SRF layers and business verticals. Shared catalog: sector instruments apply to one vertical; cited cross-cutting instruments list the verticals that map them; uncited horizontal instruments may list all six. Includes EU AI Act, NIST AI RMF, ISO 42001, OECD AI Principles, national reference instruments (UK/China/Singapore/Canada/Japan/Australia/Korea/Brazil/India), SEC/OCC/FINRA finance anchors, California AB 2013, and sector instruments. Each item carries jurisdiction, optional mapping_key, depth, and applicable_verticals. depth full means the text was read against the primary source, so the item records last_verified; depth reference means it carries verification_status instead. lifecycle is absent for an instrument in force and set to draft or rescinded otherwise, and a rescinded item names its replacement in superseded_by.

Moral orientation tags for concrete regulatory requirements. Each requirement carries independent 0-3 salience on actor (character/duties), action (deontological process/bans), and outcome (consequentialist impacts), with a required rationale. Priority instruments include EU AI Act, OECD AI Principles, NIST AI RMF, SR 26-2, GDPR, HIPAA Security Rule, UK AI white paper, China GenAI measures, Canada ADM, CMMC 2.0, SEC PDA conflicts, Korea AI Basic Act, and Australia AI Ethics Principles. Instrument-level rollups (max salience per dimension) and ontology edges are derived by the knowledge-layer generator. Descriptive analytical lens, not a claim that any country is one moral type.

40 controls for financial services AI deployments. Each control maps to an SRF layer (L1-L5), accountable persona, applicable operating models, and evidence thresholds. Regulatory context: SR 26-2, FINOS AIGF, OWASP LLM Top 10, EU AI Act. Four MRM stages: development, validation, deployment, monitoring.

40 controls for healthcare AI deployments including clinical decision support, AI-assisted diagnostics, and agentic care coordination. Each control maps to an SRF layer (L1-L5), accountable persona, clinical lifecycle stage, and FHIR AuditEvent evidence pointer. Regulatory context: FDA TPLC, FDA PCCP, ONC HTI-1, HIPAA, EU AI Act, IEC 62304, ISO 14971.

40 controls for insurance AI deployments covering underwriting, claims, and vendor model governance. Each control maps to an SRF layer (L1-L5), accountable persona, and lifecycle stage. Regulatory context: NAIC AI Model Bulletin, Colorado Regulation 10-1-1 (July 2026 deadline), NYDFS CL 7, NAIC AI Systems Evaluation Tool.

40 controls for federal civilian agency (FCEB) AI deployments. Each control maps to an SRF layer (L1-L5), accountability split (agency vs. vendor), and federal lifecycle stage. Regulatory context: OMB M-25-21 (September 22, 2026 deadline), OMB M-25-22, FedRAMP 20x KSIs, NIST AI RMF.

53 controls for DoD components and the defense industrial base. Each control maps to an SRF layer (L1-L5), impact level (IL4/IL5/IL6), NSS vs. Non-NSS tier, accountable persona, and responsibility split. Regulatory context: DoD Responsible AI tenets, CMMC 2.0, DoD CC SRG, NIST 800-171.

45 controls for manufacturing AI deployments covering OT/ICS, product-embedded AI, and IT-side manufacturing. Each control maps to an SRF layer (L1-L5), OT applicability, EU AI Act risk class, and lifecycle stage. Regulatory context: EU AI Act high-risk obligations (August 2026), EU Machinery Regulation 2023/1230 (January 2027), IEC 62443, ISO 42001.

Threat-to-accountability crosswalk. The sixteen OWASP AI Exchange security-matrix threats, each mapped to the SRF layer where it lands and the accountable persona per operating model. Includes external IDs (OWASP LLM Top 10 2025, MITRE ATLAS, BIML LLM24) and related vertical control IDs. Threat definitions and severity belong to their external sources; this file adds who authorizes, who owns each finding, and who signs residual risk.

Finding routing reference. Twenty layer-by-operating-model entries resolving an AIVSS- or CVSS-scored finding to one accountable persona and a kebab-case breach-action escalation ladder across four severity bands (critical, high, medium, low). Closes the loop opened by the threat crosswalk and the red team scoping tool. The SRF does not score severity; AIVSS and CVSS own that.

Seven AI vendor categories for vendor risk and procurement, each mapped to SRF layers, operating models, and roles, with the vendor-vs-customer accountability split, attestation baseline, and evidence to demand. Also includes a three-tier risk model, eight cross-cutting AI risks, and an attestation reference (what SOC 2, ISO 27001, ISO 42001, ISO 9001, FedRAMP, NIST AI RMF, and the EU AI Act do and do not prove).

87 classic security engineering principles, axioms, and invariables normalized from an OSCAL catalog of 93 controls. Covers Saltzer and Schroeder, NIST SP 800-27, ISO 27001, CIS Controls v8/v8.1, Microsoft's two law sets, and cloud architecture corollaries. Each entry carries a stable id, category, source citations back to the originating framework, and related links to connected principles. Baseline checklist for assessing AI security whitepapers.

121 contemporary AI and agentic security principles normalized from a 41-source synthesis (BIML, CIS, CSA, CoSAI, NIST, OWASP, SANS, 2019 to 2026) across 22 topic sections. Includes a gap_index resolving each section's Gap note to the classic principle it points at, and the source documents that assert each claim. Current industry positions rather than settled axioms.

PROPOSALS, NOT ACCEPTED PRINCIPLES. Review queue for candidate principles surfaced by whitepaper assessments, so each is triaged once with the reasoning recorded rather than re-proposed at every future review. Every entry carries a status, an evidentiary tier for its source, and closest_existing links to the catalog entries it was checked against. Do not cite an entry here as an established principle. The accepted catalogs are security-principles.json and ai-agentic-principles.json.

layers.L1: AI Business & Usage: governance, strategy, and compliance
layers.L2: AI Information: data ownership, quality, and privacy
layers.L3: AI Application: development, integration, and testing
layers.L4: AI Platform: infrastructure, APIs, and runtime services
layers.L5: AI Model Provider: foundation models and model governance

join_hints.preferred_path: Load /ontology/edges.json and join on source/target IDs from /ids.json. Do not invent a parallel edges file under /data/.
join_hints.control_id_collision: The short control id (e.g. SRF-L1-ACQ-001) repeats across verticals. The canonical form is srf.control.<vertical>.<id>.

associations.join: control.mappings.<mapping_key> cites a non-placeholder string; regulations.json item.mapping_key equals that key
regulations.json item.superseded_by, present only where lifecycle is rescinded
control.operating_models[] for the four canonical models
requirements[].moral_profile with salience 1-3 as an edge property
regulations[].applicable_verticals (prefer derived-from-controls when mapping citations exist; else declared sector or cross-cutting)

exports.description: Flattened, linked knowledge pack of the whole framework for bulk ingestion: concepts, relationships, definitions.
Glossary export companion to the knowledge pack.
Ontology export companion to the knowledge pack.

Accountability matrix as a flat CSV: one row per SRF layer (L1-L5) by operating model (AI-SaaS, AI-PaaS, Agent-PaaS, IaaS) with customer and provider responsibility. For ingestion into GRC and spreadsheet tools.

OSCAL 1.1.2 catalog of the SRF accountability matrix. Groups are SRF layers; controls are layer-by-operating-model accountability cells with customer and provider responsibility props. For ingestion into OSCAL-aware GRC platforms.
Machine-readable AI incident response playbooks: seven boundary-failure scenarios with SRF layer mapping, who-leads-by-operating-model, triage steps, vendor asks, and evidence to preserve.

OSCAL 1.2.2 catalog of all 258 industry vertical controls, grouped by SRF layer (L1-L5) with one subgroup per vertical. Each control carries the accountability assignment, a threshold parameter, regulatory mapping links, and evidence pointers. Proposed extension; not part of the official CoSAI release. Generated from data/*-controls.json.
